name: approve
description: Decide one action: approve, skip or edit its draft. Approving runs it as the product's owner and publishes or sends through the accounts connected on hustlin.ai. The founder's own post (queue_post) with a scheduledFor still ahead is the exception: approving keeps it waiting and it posts at that time

name: run
description: Execute an action that is already approved (by the founder, the team or autopilot) ahead of its scheduled slot, through the same path as the web app: leases, spend ceilings and platform policy apply, and it publishes through the owner's connected accounts. Refuses a draft that has not been approved.

name: results
description: Per channel: what Hustlin did and what it produced (attempts, reach, credited signups, purchases, revenue) last week and over four weeks, the learning loop's do-more and stop lists, and tracked-link clicks by channel. Credited means a signup or sale that came through a Hustlin tracked link.

name: report

name: connect
description: The browser URLs for connecting the accounts Hustlin posts from (X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, Google and Meta ads, email) and for tracking. Account connections happen in the browser, never through this server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "run" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "conversion_snippet" references sensitive artifacts (env var, secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: plan · Private data: conversion_snippet · Public sink: actions, queue_post, approve, connect · Destructive: actions, approve, run, conversion_snippet.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: plan · Private data: conversion_snippet · Public sink: actions, queue_post, approve, connect · Destructive: actions, approve, run, conversion_snippet

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
